projects.description:
UN Habitat:
"1. Develop capacities and establish conditions to adapt to the adverse effects of climate change in vulnerable cities of Malawi (Zomba)
 2. Protect livelihoods through enhanced all-inclusive disaster preparedness in urban centres of Blantyre, Zomba, Lilongwe and Mzuzu cities in Malawi enabled by context-specific interventions at community, city and national levels that establish risk informed urban early warning systems linked to and enabling early action.                                                
3. Implementation of Waste SDGs through African Clean Cities Platform (JFY 2022)
4. Improvement of Solid Waste Management in Zomba through waste management centres and procurement of a tractor. 
5. Develop policy documents for building urban resilience, with focus on climate-related risk.                                                                                    
 6. Develop guidelines for promoting the green cities concept, with emphasis on climate adaptation.

UNCDF:
- "1.        Increase district access to climate finance to implement climate change investments  in Malawi
2.        Establish and institutionalise a standard and internationally recognised country mechanism for PBCRGs in Malawi.
3.        Support target Districts to integrate climate risk considerations in local development policies, plans, projects and actions
4.        Support the inclusion of performance Measures for climate change in the Local Authority Performance Assessment (LAPA), including support to the annual Local Annual Performance Assessment (LAPA), Quality Assurance, training of teams for assessment, preparations of LGs etc.
5. Support to the GoM to unlock various sources of climate finance for the further deployment of the mechanism, including preparation of concept notes and project proposal with the Government of Malawi.
"

"i)Develop guidelines and regulations to support operationalisation of 2023 DRM Act.

3) WFP will remain a key provider of corridor services for humanitarian operations in the region. It will continue to engage local food suppliers and logistics service providers, stimulating local  rkets and economies."

- Provide guidance on planning and implementation of WASH improvements as part of wider quality improvement (QI) efforts, and to meet local, national and global standards; supports the implementation of IPC standard and transmission-based precautions according to national guidelines and standard operating procedures (SOPs); and facilitates multisectoral actions by bringing together all those who share responsibility for providing WASH services, including legislators and policymakers, district health officers, hospital administrators, water and sanitation engineers, climate and environmental specialists, and users.
- Support develop institutional frameworks, stakeholder participation, and sectoral engagement, implementation of climate resilient water safety plans, strengthening the climate resilience and environmental sustainability of health care facilities, integrating climate and weather variables into health surveillance systems, and building capacity on climate change and health at the local and national level.


WFP:
"1) Sustainable land and water management activities – including soil and water conservation, afforestation, water harvesting, flood control and soil fertility measures – which enhance productivity, improve water availability, reduce loss of biodiversity and decrease vulnerability to climate shocks and other stressors.
2) Rehabilitation of irrigation schemes and water source development for domestic, agricultural, livestock and aquaculture use; land rehabilitation; forestry and agroforestry management and practices. 
3) Income generation activities linked to the conservation and management of natural resources (e.g. small nursery development, compost making, beekeeping, etc.), and disaster preparedness. 
4) Microinsurance (crop insurance) support to households with a protective safety net to cope with climatic shocks through timely payouts and stimulates investment in more resilient livelihoods."
5) Provide food assistance, nutrition and livelihood support to populations in anticipation of and
response to seasonal or other shocks, leveraging national social protection systems where possible
6) Provide food and nutrition assistance, services and livelihood support to refugees, asylum
seekers and host communities"

FAO:
- (i) Support implementation of sustainable land and water use management practices (ii) Support farming households who adopted climate smart adaptation and mitigation practices in agriculture

UN Women
"  Support national efforts for disaggregated data collection and reporting under the Sendai Monitor.
•  Support the financial sector to develop innovative financing products for women’s MSMEs and start-ups. 
•  Collaborate with Ministry of Gender and DoDMA to develop guidance on strengthening women’s leadership in resilience building.
•  Support the development and implementation of the National Gender Action Plan (GAP) for the Sendai Framework.
• Support gender analysis and provide technical advice and capacity development for government officials to ensure gender-responsive, inclusive, and accessible preparedness planning, and early warning systems.
•  Facilitate access to entrepreneurship in the sustainable energy sector for women and girls’ small and medium enterprises by supporting access to credit and solar energy. 
"

UNDP:
- "i) Support Protection and restoration works in the key identified catchments areas and wetlands for enhanced ecosystem services. 
 Ii)Improved agricultural practices, soil and water conservation in production landscapes
 iii) Develope EbA Plans — with an integrated management framework that identifies climate change vulnerability and ecosystem degradation hotspots — building on Watershed Management Plans (WMPs).
 iv) Support the design and implementation of innovative and transformative DRM measures, including ECO - DRR 
 v) Support the development and dissemination of products and platforms for climate related information/services. 
 vi) Expansion of networks that generate climate related data to serve lives and livelihood from extreme climate events 
 vii) Support the development pf tools and mechanisms for climate change, DRM and ERM"

UNEP: 
Support the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) process by strengthening institutional frameworks, integrating adaptation into government spending, mobilizing private finance, and promoting knowledge sharing.

children.description:
Agency Name: World Health Organization
Key Achievements:
1) WHO technically and financially supported the monitoring and mentorship on Multi drug resistant Tuberculosis patient service delivery. The capacity built during the mentorship will benefit the 110 recent Multi drug resistant patients registered in Malawi. 

2) WHO financially supported expansion of PEN Plus services in the country, this will benefit over 6 million Malawians who have at least a Non-Communicable Disease.

3) WHO technically and financially supported training of 8 Clinicians in the management of rhodesiense Human African Trypanosomiasis (rHAT) using the new drug Fexinidazole. The skilled gained will benefit all rHAT Patients in Malawi since Clinicians were drawn from all the HAT districts of Nkhotakota, Ntchisi, Kasungu and Rumphi.

4) WHO supported MOH with 4018 filarial test strips for Post Elimination surveillance of Lymphatic Filariasis, 48 of the 4018 school going pupils tested positive and benefited from treatment.

Key Bottlenecks: Inadequate funding to implement all planned activities.
Lessons Learnt: 1) Any little support to the most vulnerable and marginalized population groups, makes a little difference.
                              2) It is important to link up for partnership support
Emerging Priorities: Need to amend policies and guidelines to include Gender, Equity and Human Rights so that no one is left behind from the planning stage to implementation.
